claims.quote: Pathogenic PRRT2 variants cause self-limited (familial) infantile epilepsy (SeLIE)
which is responsive to sodium channel blocking antiseizure medications.
Oxcarbazepine was commenced in two infants and was effective.
Eight infants were initially treated with levetiracetam, and all were subsequently switched to oxcarbazepine due to ongoing seizures or side effects.

claims.object_text: Posterior polymorphic focal epileptiform discharges on a peri-ictal EEG recording
claims.quote: Posterior polymorphic focal epileptiform discharges on a peri-ictal EEG recording are a feature of PRRT2-related SeLIE.
The interictal EEG is typically normal.

claims.object_text: focal seizures at a median age of 5 months (range: 3-6 months)
claims.quote: Ten infants presented with focal seizures at a median age of 5 months (range: 3-6 months).

claims.object_text: family history of epilepsy, paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia (PKD) or hemiplegic migraine
claims.quote: Eight had a family history of epilepsy, paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia (PKD) or hemiplegic migraine.

claims.object_text: epileptiform discharges within 24 h of most recent seizure
claims.quote: Seven of the eight infants with an EEG performed within 24 h of the most recent seizure had epileptiform discharges.

claims.object_text: focal sharp waves, spikes, polyspikes or fast activity independently over the left and right temporo-occipital regions
claims.quote: Their EEGs showed focal sharp waves, spikes, polyspikes or fast activity independently over the left and right temporo-occipital regions.

claims.object_text: no epileptiform discharges when last known seizure >24 h prior to EEG
claims.quote: Conversely, the two infants with last known seizure greater than 24 h prior to their EEG had no epileptiform discharges.
